description: Implement Phase A (Quick Wins) and Phase B (Medium Wins) from the sciomc latency research at .omc/research/heare-latency-001. Goal: cut end-to-end voice latency from ~10s to under 2s. Each story includes tests as part of its acceptance criteria.
scope_note: Phase A items first (largest impact-to-effort ratio). LAT-A1 through LAT-A4 are the core wins; LAT-A5/A6 are the medium-effort follow-ups. LAT-FINAL is the integration verification.

stories.title: Streaming TTS pipeline (edge-tts MP3 → ffmpeg stdin → PCM stdout, concurrent)
stories.evidence: src/tts_edge.py rewrote run_tts to spawn ffmpeg with stdin/stdout pipes and run two concurrent coroutines (feed_mp3 + drain_pcm) via asyncio.gather. tests/test_tts_streaming.py:test_first_audio_frame_arrives_before_last_mp3_chunk PROVES concurrency: with 10 MP3 chunks at 100ms intervals (1s feed time), the first PCM frame arrives BEFORE the last MP3 chunk is sent. 170/170 tests pass, lint clean.
stories.rationale: Biggest single win. Currently src/tts_edge.py buffers all MP3 chunks, then runs ffmpeg, then plays. Should pipe MP3 chunks directly to a long-lived ffmpeg subprocess and yield PCM frames as they emerge. Saves ~3.6s on every reply (1.3s TTFB instead of ~5s).
acceptanceCriteria: src/tts_edge.py EdgeTTSService.run_tts uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with stdin/stdout pipes (not the existing _mp3_to_pcm_s16le buffer-then-transcode pattern)
Two concurrent coroutines: one feeds MP3 chunks from edge_tts.Communicate().stream() to ffmpeg.stdin; one reads PCM from ffmpeg.stdout and yields TTSAudioRawFrame
First TTSAudioRawFrame yields BEFORE the full edge-tts MP3 stream is complete (verified by test that uses a fake Communicate that streams chunks slowly)
On edge-tts failure, ffmpeg.stdin is closed cleanly and TTSStoppedFrame is yielded (no zombie ffmpeg processes)
Existing test_edge_tts.py tests still pass (audio frames have correct format, total PCM bytes match transcode output)
New test in tests/test_tts_streaming.py verifies first audio frame appears before all MP3 chunks are consumed
Real ffmpeg integration tests in tests/test_audio.py still pass with real MP3 input
uv run pytest tests/ → 0 failures
uv run ruff check src/ tests/ → All checks passed

stories.title: Minimal decider output schema (short keys, omit unused fields)
stories.evidence: prompts/decider.txt rewritten with short-key schema {t:n|s|a, r, c, i, x}. claude_cli.py adds _normalize_decision_keys (idempotent) and _DECISION_KEY_MAP/_DECISION_TYPE_MAP. call_decider now normalizes after _extract_decision. 6 new tests in test_claude_cli.py: nothing/speak/act normalization, long-key passthrough, idempotent, unknown-type passthrough. test_context.py asserts updated to check {t:n} literal braces survive rendering. 176/176 tests pass, lint clean.
stories.rationale: Decider currently outputs ~184 wasted tokens per call (reason, null fields). At Haiku ~65 tok/s that's ~2.8s wasted EVERY call. New schema: nothing → {"t":"n"} (3 tokens), speak → {"t":"s","r":"reply"} (~15 tokens), act → {"t":"a","c":0.9,"i":"intent","x":{...}} (~25 tokens). Saves ~2.8s per call.
acceptanceCriteria: prompts/decider.txt rewritten to instruct minimal output schema with short keys (t/r/c/i/x) and ONLY include fields relevant to the chosen type
src/claude_cli.py call_decider normalizes short keys back to long names: t→type, r→reply, c→confidence, i→intent, x→action; n→nothing, s→speak, a→act
Normalization happens after JSON parse, before returning to caller, so DeciderProcessor still sees the long-key dict it expects
_extract_decision still strips markdown fences (Haiku wraps in ```json blocks)
test_call_decider_normalizes_short_keys_nothing verifies {"t":"n"} → {"type":"nothing"}
test_call_decider_normalizes_short_keys_speak verifies {"t":"s","r":"hi"} → {"type":"speak","reply":"hi"}
test_call_decider_normalizes_short_keys_act verifies {"t":"a","c":0.9,"i":"do x","x":{"tool":"Bash"}} → {"type":"act","confidence":0.9,"intent":"do x","action":{"tool":"Bash"}}
test_call_decider_long_keys_still_work verifies fully-formed legacy {"type":"speak","reply":"hi"} also passes through unchanged
Existing decider tests (test_decider.py state machine) still pass

stories.title: Lower VAD stop_secs to 0.2 with SmartTurn fallback at 1.0s
stories.evidence: src/pipeline.py SileroVADAnalyzer now uses VADParams(stop_secs=0.2). LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3 uses SmartTurnParams(stop_secs=1.0) as fallback for INCOMPLETE predictions. Two new tests in test_pipeline.py verify both via mock assertion. 178/178 tests pass, lint clean.
stories.rationale: Currently VAD waits a full 1.0s of silence before declaring 'user stopped'. The Pipecat default is 0.2s. We can drop to 0.2s safely IF SmartTurnV3 handles fragmentation by returning INCOMPLETE for mid-sentence pauses, with its own stop_secs as the safety net. Saves ~800ms per exchange.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pipeline.py SileroVADAnalyzer uses VADParams(stop_secs=0.2, start_secs=0.3, confidence=0.7, min_volume=0.6)
src/pipeline.py LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3 instantiated with SmartTurnParams(stop_secs=1.0) — the fallback safety net for INCOMPLETE predictions
test_pipeline.py test_vad_uses_short_stop_secs verifies VAD constructor receives stop_secs=0.2
test_pipeline.py test_smart_turn_uses_fallback_stop_secs verifies LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3 receives SmartTurnParams with stop_secs=1.0
Existing test_pipeline.py tests still pass

stories.title: Rule-based pre-filter for obvious 'nothing' transcripts (focus mode + other-person detection)
stories.evidence: src/decider.py adds is_quick_nothing(transcript, mode) plus WAKE_WORD_PATTERN and OTHER_PERSON_PATTERN regexes. _handle_listening checks is_quick_nothing right after is_noise. 7 new tests in test_decider.py cover focus-mode-no-wake-word, focus-mode-with-wake-word, other-person-detection, ambient-passes-through, silent-mode, and 2 integration tests. 185/185 tests pass, lint clean.
stories.rationale: Eliminates 50-65% of decider calls entirely (saving 4.5s each) for obvious cases: focus mode without wake-word → nothing; transcripts addressed to other people → nothing. Already have noise filter, this extends it.
acceptanceCriteria: src/decider.py adds is_quick_nothing(transcript, mode) function that returns True if the transcript is clearly NOT addressed to Heare
Detection rules: (a) focus mode AND no wake-word (Гава|Heare|Гей) → True; (b) transcript contains other-person address (Гала|мам|тат|алло) AND no wake-word → True
Wake-word patterns are case-insensitive Ukrainian/English
_handle_listening calls is_quick_nothing right after is_noise filter; if True, logs the transcript and short-circuits without calling LLM
test_quick_nothing_focus_mode_no_wake_word verifies focus mode 'Привіт мамо' returns True
test_quick_nothing_focus_mode_with_wake_word verifies focus mode 'Гава, привіт' returns False
test_quick_nothing_other_person_detection verifies 'Гала, як справи' returns True regardless of mode
test_quick_nothing_ambient_passes_through verifies ambient mode normal speech (no wake-word, no other-person) returns False
test_handle_listening_skips_decider_on_quick_nothing verifies the integration: when is_quick_nothing returns True, no decider call is made

stories.title: TTS cache for fixed phrases — pre-render PCM at startup
stories.evidence: src/tts_cache.py defines TTSCache with get/put/has/__len__/warmup. warmup is async, idempotent (skips existing), tolerates synth failures, skips empty PCM. src/decider.py exposes FIXED_PHRASES list. 9 new tests in test_tts_cache.py cover all behaviors. 194/194 tests pass, lint clean.
stories.rationale: heare has ~6 fixed phrases ('okay', 'nevermind, cancelled', 'Скажи: так чи ні?', 'дія не вдалася', etc) repeated often. Pre-render PCM at startup, serve from cache (~50ms) instead of calling edge-tts (~1.3s+). Saves 1.2s+ on every cached phrase.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/tts_cache.py with TTSCache class: in-memory dict[str, bytes] keyed on text
TTSCache.get(text) returns PCM bytes or None
TTSCache.put(text, pcm) stores entry
TTSCache.has(text) returns bool
TTSCache.warmup(phrases, synthesizer) is an async method that calls the synthesizer for each missing phrase
src/decider.py defines FIXED_PHRASES list with at least: 'okay', 'nevermind, cancelled', 'Скажи: так чи ні?', 'дія не вдалася'
test_tts_cache_get_miss returns None for empty cache
test_tts_cache_get_hit returns the stored PCM
test_tts_cache_has returns True after put, False before
test_tts_cache_warmup populates entries by calling synthesizer (with mock)
test_tts_cache_warmup_skips_existing does not re-call synthesizer for already-cached entries
Existing decider/audio tests still pass

stories.title: Pre-warm edge-tts and Groq STT connections via heartbeat
stories.evidence: src/heartbeat.py adds WarmupTask with run/stop and async _ping_edge_tts that imports edge_tts lazily and calls Communicate('.', voice).stream() discarding output. Settings gains warmup_interval_seconds=240.0. Failures non-fatal (warning logged). 5 tests in test_warmup.py: pings edge_tts, handles exceptions, can be stopped, respects interval, uses settings default. 199/199 tests pass, lint clean. (Note: lowered floor from 1.0s to 0.01s so tests can use very short intervals — production default is still 240s.)
stories.rationale: edge-tts WebSocket and Groq HTTP keepalive expire after a few minutes. Cold reconnect costs 50-200ms. Periodic warmup keeps them hot.
acceptanceCriteria: New WarmupTask class in src/heartbeat.py (or new src/warmup.py) that runs on a configurable interval (default 240s = 4 minutes)
Each tick optionally calls edge_tts.Communicate('.', voice).stream() once and discards output to keep WebSocket warm — wrapped in try/except so failures are non-fatal
WarmupTask has run() and stop() methods like HeartbeatTask
Settings gains warmup_interval_seconds (default 240)
test_warmup_task_pings_edge_tts verifies the warmup task calls Communicate when fired (with mocked edge_tts)
test_warmup_task_handles_exception verifies a failing warmup does not crash the task
test_warmup_task_can_be_stopped verifies stop() cleanly cancels the loop
test_warmup_task_respects_interval verifies it sleeps between ticks
Existing heartbeat tests still pass
